## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished presentation. To learn more about Quarto presentations see <https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/>.

## Bullets

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes:

-   Content authored with markdown
-   Output from executable code

## Code

When you click the **Render** button a presentation will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

# Load packages

```{r}
pacman::p_load(rio, here, tidyverse, ggsci, ggrepel, ggpubr, grid, ggh4x)
```

# Import data

```{r}
data_inc_latam <- import(here("data", "clean", "dataset-asr-inc-age-20-69-latam.csv"))

data_inc_no_latam <- import(here("data", "clean", "dataset-asr-inc-age-20-69-no-latam.csv"))

data_mor_latam <- import(here("data", "clean", "dataset-asr-mort-age-20-69-latam.csv"))

data_mor_no_latam <- import(here("data", "clean", "dataset-asr-mort-age-20-69-no-latam.csv"))
```

# Incidence LATAM

```{r}
data_inc_latam <- data_inc_latam |>
  mutate(
    Sex = factor(Sex) |> 
      fct_recode("Varones" = "1", "Mujeres" = "2"))

# Crear dataframe de breaks y labels para el eje secundario
sec_y <- data_inc_latam |>
  filter(Year == max(Year)) |>
  select(`ASR (World)`, Sex) |>
  setNames(c("breaks", "labels"))

# Gráfico con eje secundario etiquetado y coloreado
F1 <- ggplot(
  data = data_inc_latam, 
  aes(x = factor(Year), y = `ASR (World)`, color = Sex, group = Sex)
  ) +
  geom_point(size = 2, shape = 19) +
  geom_smooth(size = 1.2, se = FALSE, method = "loess", span = 0.30) +
  scale_y_continuous(sec.axis = dup_axis(breaks = sec_y$breaks, labels = sec_y$labels)) +
  ggsci::scale_color_lancet() +
  ggpubr::theme_classic2() +
  ggpubr::labs_pubr() +
  labs(
    y = "Tasa estandarizada por edad (por 100,000)", 
    title = "Incidencia en América Latina") +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.major = element_line(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(),
    axis.text.y.right = element_text(color = pal_lancet(palette = "lanonc")(2)),
    axis.title.y.right = element_blank(),
    axis.line.y.right = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks.y.right = element_blank(),
    axis.title.x = element_blank()
  )

## Save the combined plot as a PNG file
ggplot2::ggsave(
  plot = F1,
  filename = here::here("outputs", "LATAM_incidence.png"),
  width = 7,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 300,
  units = "in")
```

F5 <- ggarrange(F1, F2, F3, F4, ncol = 4, nrow = 1)
